cse-2014-3-cs-35.approach: Recall the standard decidability results for CFGs: membership, emptiness and finiteness all have algorithms; ambiguity does not (it reduces from the Post Correspondence Problem).

steps.title: Decidable CFG problems
steps.body:
- **Membership** $w \in L(G)$: CYK algorithm, $O(|w|^3)$.
- **Emptiness**: mark useful (generating) variables; $L(G)=\emptyset$ iff $S$ is not generating.
- **Finiteness**: convert to CNF, remove useless symbols, and check the variable-dependency graph for a cycle.

steps.title: Undecidable problem
steps.body: Given a PCP instance one can build a grammar $G$ that is ambiguous **iff** the PCP instance has a solution. Since PCP is undecidable, so is CFG ambiguity.

answer.value: Deciding whether a CFG is ambiguous

optionAnalysis.reason: Correct — ambiguity of CFGs is undecidable (reduction from PCP).
Decidable — CYK decides membership in $O(n^3)$.
Decidable — check whether the start symbol derives some terminal string.
Decidable — after cleaning the grammar, $L(G)$ is infinite iff the dependency graph has a cycle.

pitfalls: Equivalence and universality ($L(G)=\Sigma^*$) of CFGs are also undecidable, but finiteness is decidable.
cse-2014-3-cs-35.verification: Standard table of CFL decision properties: membership, emptiness, finiteness decidable; ambiguity undecidable.

cse-2014-3-cs-36.approach: Ask whether a DPDA can know when to switch from pushing to popping. With an explicit marker (block of 1s, or the centre symbol c) it can; for $ww^r$ the middle must be guessed, which needs nondeterminism.

steps.title: $L_1=\{0^n1^n\}$
steps.body: Push for every 0; on the first 1 start popping one per 1; accept on reaching the bottom marker. The 0→1 boundary is visible, so the PDA is deterministic. **DCFL.**

steps.title: $L_2=\{wcw^r\}$
steps.body: Push every symbol of $w$; on reading $c$ switch to matching mode and pop-compare each symbol of $w^r$. The centre marker $c$ tells the machine exactly when to switch. **DCFL.**

steps.title: $L_3=\{ww^r\}$
steps.body: Even-length palindromes over $\{0,1\}$ have no marker for the middle; the PDA must guess it. $L_3$ is a CFL but **not** a DCFL (classic result: after reading $0^n110^n$ a DPDA would have to both accept and still be able to continue correctly on $0^n110^n0^n110^n$).

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.body: Only $L_1$ and $L_2$ are deterministic CFLs.

Wrong — $L_2$ is also deterministic thanks to the centre marker $c$.
Correct — $L_1$, $L_2$ are DCFLs; $L_3$ needs a nondeterministic guess of the middle.
Wrong — $ww^r$ is not a DCFL.

pitfalls: Confusing $wcw^r$ (marked palindrome, DCFL) with $ww^r$ (unmarked, non-deterministic CFL).
cse-2014-3-cs-36.verification: Standard examples: $wcw^R$ is the textbook DCFL, $ww^R$ the textbook CFL that is not a DCFL.

steps.body: $\Phi$ is unsatisfiable $\iff$ for some $i$, $x_i$ reaches $\overline{x_i}$ **and** $\overline{x_i}$ reaches $x_i$. This is directed-graph reachability (or one SCC computation): polynomial, in fact linear.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.body: 2CNFSAT $\in$ P, solved by reduction to directed-graph reachability.
